text: The correction reported that spec/F-0168 does not rebase cleanly onto main, conflicting in tests/test_s1_gate.py. I verified this directly: `git rebase origin/main` on the branch conflicts at commit 4f5809619, which had added a `since()` helper to de-date-bomb `test_an_undecided_s1_holds_nothing`. Main independently landed the same fix in 5f76f3ed2 (PR #321, "test(s1-gate): the undecided age is relative to the clock, not a fixed date") with different variable naming, so the two edits collide textually though they're semantically identical. The branch's very next commit, 035a68dcf, had already reverted 4f5809619's change wholesale ("drop the test fix — main already carries it") on the theory that main's fix supersedes it — correct in outcome, but leaving both commits in the branch's history still causes rebase to choke on the now-dead intermediate edit before the revert ever applies. Upheld: I confirmed `git diff 8ab210a55 HEAD -- tests/test_s1_gate.py` was empty (the two commits net to zero), then collapsed them out of the branch's history (`git reset --soft` to 8ab210a55, the commit before both), leaving the branch touching only docs/specs/f-0168.md. Verified in a throwaway branch that `git rebase origin/main` now applies with zero conflicts and that `tests/test_s1_gate.py`'s 5 tests pass green in that rebased state, inheriting main's own fix untouched. Nothing else was in dispute — no review file exists for round 1, and the spec document itself never named or depended on the S1-gate test, so this was pure history cleanup, not a content change. This finding does not come back: the branch's local history has been rewritten to drop the redundant test-fix/revert pair, and per the job's own rule a non-fast-forward push here is expected and left for the factory to publish.

There was no review file and no docs/plans/f-0167.md ever committed (checked git log --all — nothing on any branch), so the "3 PLAN sessions starved" hold had no recorded finding to uphold or overrule; the dispute was implicit. I re-verified every P1-P25 anchor and the whole quota chain against current origin/main (18233ccfd..56101f560): zero drift, nothing moved. I then traced the design's own module-global `_MEMO` (needed so one `asf status` render shares a reading across its six call sites, D1) against the actual test tree, and found what most plausibly explains the starvation: three test classes — `TestStatusShowsStale` (tests/test_quota_stale.py:181-206), `TestStatusCell` (tests/test_quota_headroom.py:332-350), and `StatusViewTests`' two quota-cell tests (tests/test_views.py:205-221) — run several methods in one process against the same account name, each re-mocking `CommandQuotaSource.read` to a different reading; wrapped in `CachedQuotaSource` as designed, the second and third method of each class would silently read the first method's memo instead of its own mock. P18 had certified "one method the cache can surprise" by checking only for re-mocking *inside* one method, not reuse *across* methods of one class in one process — a correctness gap invisible without tracing the actual fixtures, exactly the shape of finding a PLAN session can burn its whole budget chasing (or three, independently, without ever converging on a commit). Upheld and fixed directly: added P26 (the measured collision) and D12 (the fix — `HomeCase.setUp` and `ViewsTestCase.setUp` each gain one `quota.forget()` call, reusing the `forget()` D6 already names for "a test between two mocked readings"), threaded through the `## In` bullets, the `CachedQuotaSource` design section, and a new acceptance-test line naming the four now-guarded methods. Nothing else in the spec was found wrong; it is overruled as a whole only in the sense that "the spec is unplannable" does not hold — it was planizable minus this one gap, which is now closed. The item is unblocked and should proceed to PLAN.
